sources.entry: Mailspring - 💌 A beautiful, fast and maintained fork of @nylas Mail by one of the original authors

summary.one_liner: Mailspring is a desktop email client, a maintained fork of Nylas Mail, built with Electron, React and TypeScript on a C++ sync engine.
summary.what_it_does: Mailspring is a desktop email client that its README describes as a new version of Nylas Mail, maintained by one of the original authors. The UI is written in TypeScript with Electron and React and is built on a plugin architecture. Its sync engine is a C++ and C program based on Mailcore2 that runs locally on the user's machine and replaces the JavaScript sync code from Nylas Mail. Built-in features named in the README include a Unified Inbox, Snooze, Send Later, Mail Rules and Templates. Mailspring Pro, a monthly subscription, adds link tracking, read receipts, mailbox analytics and contact and company profiles. The README says features run in the client and credentials are not sent to the cloud. Users can also build plugins and themes, and localization is supported from version 1.5.0.
use_cases: Read and manage email on the desktop
Build a custom email plugin or theme
Use email templates and mail rules
how_to_run: export npm_config_arch=x64 # If you are on an M1 / Apple Silicon Mac
notable: Replaces Nylas Mail's JavaScript sync code with a C++ sync engine that the README says uses about half the RAM and CPU of Nylas Mail
Plugin architecture designed for extension, with theme and plugin starter repositories
Sync engine runs locally, and the client does not send email credentials to the cloud
Ships compiled builds for Windows, Mac OS X and Linux (deb, rpm, snap)
caveats: Advanced features such as link tracking and read receipts require Mailspring Pro, a paid monthly subscription
Running from source requires an npm_config_arch override on Apple Silicon Macs
A plugin store is described as coming soon; plugins currently have to be sideloaded by hand
